title: Model Avalanche Early-Warning & Response Playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: sudden shifts in the open model landscape (new high-quality entrants, regional availability outages, pricing shocks) create operational and commercial risk for Redwood customers. We lack a repeatable, instrumented playbook that detects an emergent model 'avalanche' (rapid supply or pricing change), evaluates customer impact, and automates decisioning across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.

Scope: define signals, thresholds, dashboards, decision trees, and operational runbooks (alerts, engineering tasks, procurement triggers, customer comms). Deliverables: 1) signal catalog and anomaly detectors, 2) Grafana dashboards and alert rules, 3) response runbook with stakeholder RACI, 4) automated lightweight remediation recipes (model routing adjustments, canary swaps, quota throttles), 5) procurement/partner outreach triggers.

Why now: increased frequency of provider pricing experiments and regional outages in the past 12 months; customers in regulated verticals request predictable failover contracts. This playbook reduces MTTI (mean time to mitigation) and protects unit economics during supply shocks.
acceptance_criteria: Signal catalog published with 12 prioritized signals (availability, pricing, latency spikes, model quality regressions, quantization support changes)

Two end-to-end alert-to-action flows implemented: (a) automatic routing fallback from Hosted->Dedicated on region outage; (b) automated canary swap to pre-approved equivalent model when primary model cost increases >15%
Grafana dashboards with baseline windows and alert thresholds live in staging and tied to PagerDuty escalation
Runbook approved by SRE, Sales Ops, and Legal for initial rollout (public customers & enterprise contracts)
Postmortem template and a 30-day follow-up checklist created for every triggered avalanche event
